# Measured business impact

*Generated by `python benchmarks/impact_benchmark.py --runs 20` (offline deterministic mode, no API key).*

## Headline

- **Time to a first full threat model:** ~13 ms of agent time (median across examples) vs **24-40 consultant hours** (3-5 days) for a manual engagement.
- **Realistic end-to-end effort with expert review:** 2-4 h vs 24-40 h → **83-95% less security-expert time.**
- **Cost per threat model:** ~USD 125-450 (review time only; offline mode has no API cost) vs **USD 1,500-4,500** for the consultant engagement.
- **Lead time:** minutes instead of 7-21 days to procure and schedule a consultant; the model can be re-run on every architecture change at no extra cost.
- **Coverage:** 37/38 (97%) of the expert-checklist threats found across the three examples.

### Checklist items not found

- **Masar HR & Payroll Portal**: Mass assignment of salary / role fields — The KB suppresses this because the API documents input_validation; a reviewer should still confirm explicit DTOs are used.

## Baseline assumptions (state them, then challenge them)

| Assumption | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Manual engagement length | 3-5 consultant-days | Typical scope for an SME web/mobile app: kickoff workshop, DFD, STRIDE session, write-up (author's consulting experience). |
| Consultant day rate | USD 500-900 | Assumed range for a senior AppSec consultant serving Egypt/KSA SMEs; not a market survey. |
| Procurement & scheduling lead time | 7-21 calendar days | Assumption. |
| Human review of ThreatLens output | 2-4 hours | Recommended: an engineer/consultant validates findings and closes those with existing controls. |
| Offline-mode API cost | USD 0 | Runs locally on the built-in knowledge base. LLM mode adds the provider's token cost. |

## Method & caveats

- Timing is wall-clock for the full agent loop (parse → inventory → STRIDE → flows → API → map → score → reflect → plan → diagram → report files), median of 20 runs per example on the build machine. LLM mode is slower (seconds to minutes, depending on provider and model).
- The expert checklist (`benchmarks/expected/*.yaml`) was written by the author before measuring; a checklist item counts as found when a finding carries one of its CWE ids on the expected target. It is **not** an independent ground truth. Treat recall as a sanity check, not a certification.
- Finding counts are not quality on their own: the knowledge base is deliberately conservative (undocumented controls are treated as absent), so some findings will be closed during review with evidence.
- ThreatLens replaces the *documentation and enumeration* part of a threat-modeling engagement; it does not replace penetration testing or a consultant's judgment on business-specific abuse cases.
